role.altitude: She still plans the outing, sits in the meeting, picks the books, and sets every mark. The copies that repeat fields she already wrote get shorter. Guiding students, speaking in the committee, and issuing books stay the same length.
reach: Tutors write the date, place, headcount and aim before a one-to-one outing, and they still lead it in person.
Instructional Coordinators can paste a decision sentence they already wrote; the committee meeting stays theirs.
Librarians and Media Collections Specialists keep the supplier line, and the teacher trusts ISBN, price and supplier only when that row matches the title she picked.
Adult Basic Education, Adult Secondary Education, and English as a Second Language Instructors can compare a key they wrote with letters they recorded; the grade stays theirs.
skills_to_grow: Write the activity fields before a note is copied
Keep the answer key and the closed letters as her own capture
Set the mark herself after reading any drafted comment
role.ambitious_version: A closed-item tick and a comment that cites her rubric row are ready before she sits down to grade, and she still decides the mark and leads the trip.

tasks.short: Plan a class trip or contest, then supervise it.

steps.what: Plan class projects, field trips and contests
Copy stored date, place and headcount
Give students the trip note in person
Mail the guest the agreed visit date
Supervise activities and guide students learning

tasks.design: She writes the activity type, the date, the place, the headcount, the learning aim and, for a guest visit, the guest name in the {DOCS} plan. A copy places only those stored fields on the permission note. She chooses the activity, hands the note to the students, mails the guest, and supervises the class.
tasks.previous_blocker: The date, place and headcount lived only in her head, so the permission note was a fresh composition every time.
tasks.enabler_now: Once those fields sit on the activity plan, a second writing of the same fields is a copy.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the activity, guiding students on the day, and telling the guest the plan in her own mail stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can drop a trip the group in front of her is not ready to take.
tasks.altitude: The outing and the supervision stay the same length. The shorter piece is retyping a date, a place and a headcount she already stored.

reach.learn: Write date, place, headcount and aim before the outing, and still lead it in person.

evidence.claim: A permission note that copies only a date, a place, a headcount and a guest name the teacher already typed does not decide the outing. If a learner is a minor, the parent is told about the trip. A student's name is not one of the copied fields.

assumptions: The teacher is the producer of the activity plan in s1: activity type, date, place, headcount, learning aim, and guest name. Guest name may be blank only when the activity type is not a guest visit. That capture is her time at full length. The copy in s2 writes only those stored fields. If date, place or headcount is missing, she writes the note herself and the copy does not run.

Giving the note to students, mailing the guest, and supervising the activities stay at full length. The mail is her own wording to the guest, sent by her. Nothing in this task books a class or takes payment. The in-person prior is the hand-out and the supervision. The document prior is the plan and the second copy. The mail prior is the guest mail.
Upkeep of 1 hour per 100 is keeping those field names aligned with the note. No programme-lead gate is added.
unknowns: Whether learners on these courses are minors.
Whether off-site trips need a manager sign-off at this provider.
research_questions: What fraction of outings already have a date, a place and a headcount written before the note?

already_counted.description: Planning the activity, handing out the note, mailing the guest and supervising the students, which stay at full length.

incremental.description: Keep the activity field list aligned with the permission note when the form changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when there is no second note, or when date, place or headcount was never stored and she writes the slip. High when those three fields are already on the plan and only the retype disappears. She still plans, hands the note out, mails the guest and supervises.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend staff meetings and serve on committees.

steps.what: Read the committee papers before attending
Attend staff meetings and serve on committees
Write the decision sentence in her words
Paste that stored sentence into the mail
Send that pasted mail to the committee

tasks.design: She attends the meeting and writes any decision in her own words in {DOCS}, with the meeting date. A mail step pastes only that stored sentence and the meeting date into {EMAIL}. She sends that mail herself. The paste writes no minutes and logs no attendance.
tasks.previous_blocker: The decision lived in her memory of the room, so a later mail was a new composition.
tasks.enabler_now: A sentence she has already written can be pasted without a second drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Being in the meeting, serving on the committee, choosing the sentence, and sending the mail stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can refuse to circulate a line that does not match what the room agreed.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays the same length. The shorter piece is retyping one sentence she already stored.

reach.learn: A stored decision sentence can be pasted onward; the meeting itself stays theirs.

evidence.claim: Circulating one sentence the teacher wrote, with a meeting date, does not score staff and does not record who attended. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Reading the papers is a read, at full length. Attending and serving means she speaks and decides with the people in the room, so that step is an act toward them and stays at full length. She is the producer, in s3, of the decision sentence and the meeting date. The paste writes only that sentence and that date into a draft. If she stored no sentence, she writes the mail herself and the paste does not run. She sends the mail in s5, at full length. The paste does not send it.

This design does not record attendance or session logs, so staff-monitoring consent is not the point of the change. No model writes minutes of a meeting it did not attend. The document prior is the reading and the sentence. The meeting prior is the room. The mail prior is the paste and her send.
Incremental hours are zero because there is no list and no model to keep. The paste is one sentence she already wrote.
unknowns: How often a meeting ends with one decision she is willing to write as a single sentence.
research_questions: What share of committee meetings produce a sentence she later retypes to colleagues?

already_counted.description: Reading the papers, attending the meeting and writing the decision sentence, which stay at full length.

incremental.description: No field list and no model to maintain for a paste of one stored sentence.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when she leaves with nothing she will put in a sentence, so she writes any mail herself. High when one stored sentence is pasted into the draft and she still sends that mail. The meeting, the reading, the writing of that sentence, and the send stay hers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select, order, and issue course books and supplies.

steps.what: Select books and materials for these courses
Match the chosen title to the catalogue
Read the price, supplier and edition line
Draft the order from the accepted line
Order the accepted books from the supplier
Issue books, materials and supplies in class

tasks.design: She selects the title and writes the course and the quantity in {DOCS}. The {PROCUREMENT} catalogue, which the librarian maintains, returns the ISBN, the price and the supplier for that exact title, and she reads the line before a draft may use it. She sends the order herself and issues the books, materials and supplies in class.
tasks.previous_blocker: ISBN, price and supplier were hunted across supplier lists for every title, including titles the library already held.
tasks.enabler_now: A catalogue row maintained by the librarian can return those three fields for a title she has already written.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the title, reading the returned line, sending the order and handing the books out stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can reject a catalogue row that is a different edition from the one the course needs.
tasks.altitude: Choosing titles and issuing books stay the same length. The shorter pieces are the catalogue search and the retyping of a line she has accepted.

reach.task: Keep the supplier line on a course book
reach.learn: The teacher will trust ISBN, price and supplier only when the librarian's row matches the title she picked.

evidence.claim: An order the teacher still sends, for a title she chose, does not by itself create a learner record. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The teacher is the producer, in s1, of title, course and quantity, written while she selects, at full length. The librarian is the producer of ISBN, price and supplier on the catalogue row. The match in s2 only returns that row for the exact title. If the title has no row, she searches the supplier list inside that same step and the saving does not apply. She reads the returned line in s3 at full length, and that read is her acceptance.

The draft uses only the title and quantity she wrote and the ISBN, price and supplier on the line she accepted. She still sends the order, and she still issues the books in person, both at full length. The librarian's row upkeep is the librarian's time and is not taken off her saving. The in-person prior is the selection and the issuing. The screen prior is the match and the read.
Upkeep of 1 hour per 100 is keeping the order-draft field list aligned when a supplier form changes.
unknowns: What fraction of titles are already on the librarian's catalogue with ISBN, price and supplier.
research_questions: How often is the chosen title a craft supply with no catalogue row?

already_counted.description: Selecting the title, reading the catalogue line, sending the order and issuing the books, which stay at full length.

incremental.description: Keep the order-draft field list aligned when the supplier form changes.
The librarian keeps ISBN, price and supplier on each catalogue row the teacher may match.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when craft supplies have no catalogue row and she still searches, and when she rewrites the order line after rejecting the edition. High when most titles match a librarian row, she accepts the line, and only the search and the retype shrink. She still selects, reads, sends and issues.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign class work and grade the homework.

steps.what: Assign class work and write the homework key
Record each closed letter while collecting homework
Compare stored letters with the homework key
Draft a comment that cites her rubric row

loop.input: The open answer on the collected homework, and the rubric row the teacher stored with the assignment, including that row's wording.
loop.output: A comment that restates that rubric row against a phrase that appears in the answer, and that states no mark.
loop.check: The draft restates the wording of one rubric row she stored, applied to a phrase that appears in the answer, and it states no mark and no score. A row id alone does not pass. If the draft adds a judgement or a mark, the check fails.
loop.stop: One draft. If the check fails, the draft is discarded and she writes the comment herself while she grades.
loop.why_not_simpler: A letter compare cannot restate a rubric sentence against a phrase in free text.

steps.what: Grade the open homework and set the mark
Talk that grade through with the student
File the mark she set on the pupil row

tasks.design: She assigns the work in {DOCS}, including the correct letter for each closed item and a rubric row for each open item, and she writes the student's closed letter on the {SPREADSHEET} before any compare runs. A compare records only those stored letters against her key, and a bounded draft comments on the open answer only by restating one of her rubric rows against a phrase in the answer, with no mark. She sets the mark, talks it through with the student, and only then does the {SPREADSHEET} store the mark snapshot she wrote.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed letters and the key sat on paper, so a second pass re-marked the same ticks, and a comment had no stored rubric sentence to stay inside.
tasks.enabler_now: A letter she has written can be compared with a key she has written, and a comment can be held to a rubric sentence she has stored.
tasks.still_hard: Assigning the work, recording the letters, setting the mark and talking it through stay with her. The draft can be unfair even when it cites her row.
tasks.human_edge: She can discard a comment that cites her row and still misreads the learner in front of her, and she sets the mark.
tasks.altitude: She still assigns the work and sets every mark. Closed ticks and a comment that stays inside her rubric can be waiting when she sits down. The conversation with the student stays the same length.

reach.role: Adult Basic Education, Adult Secondary Education, and English as a Second Language Instructors
reach.task: Mark closed items on an exercise
reach.learn: A key the teacher wrote can be compared to letters she recorded; the grade stays hers.

evidence.claim: AI that evaluates learning outcomes in educational or vocational institutions is high-risk, and those rules apply from 2 December 2027. This design does not have the model set or propose a mark. Whether a self-enrichment course counts as such an institution is not settled by the rule text alone.
A tutoring trial found that some suggestions were not appropriate for the learner's level.
A mark is personal data. The basis is the course contract. When the learner is a minor, parents are informed. The stored fields are learner id, assignment id, mark and date.

assumptions: The teacher is the producer, in s1, of the question, the correct option letter for each closed item, and each rubric row id and wording. She is the producer, in s2, of the student's option letter, written while she collects the homework, before the compare. The compare records a match only where that stored letter equals her key. Unkeyed items stay with her in the grade step. The comment draft may only restate a rubric row she stored, applied to a phrase in the answer, and it states no mark. The check does not prove the comment is fair. She reads every draft while she sets the mark, at full length, because suggestions can be wrong for the learner's level.

She sets every mark in s5. That mark snapshot is what s7 files, and only after s5. The file stores learner id, assignment id, mark and date. The model does not face the learner. The document prior is the assignment, the comment and the grading. The sheet prior is the letters, the compare and the file. Talking the grade through is the in-person prior and stays at full length.
Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 is keeping that four-field list and refreshing the parent notice when a learner is a minor. Rewriting a bad comment is already inside the grade step.
unknowns: Whether learners on these courses are minors.
What fraction of homework items are closed items with a letter key she stored.
research_questions: What share of homework is open writing, where she rewrites every comment and the compare has nothing to tick?

already_counted.description: Assigning the work, recording closed letters, setting the mark and talking the grade through, which stay at full length.

incremental.description: Keep the stored fields to learner id, assignment id, mark and date, and refresh the parent notice when a learner is a minor.

approvals.approved_version: mark snapshot she wrote for this assignment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when almost all homework is open writing and she rewrites every comment, so the compare and the draft save nothing. High when most items are closed, the key and the letters were both written, and she keeps the comment that restates her rubric row. She still sets every mark and talks it through.
